text.p01: To those who let their gifts flow, just like Nura. A story about generosity and the gifts we pass on.
text.p03: High on the mountain, the snow began to melt. Drip… drip… drip.
text.p04: And from the drips, a tiny spring bubbled up into the sunlight. Her name was Nura.
text.p05: Beside Nura grew a young willow named Willo. Every day, she gave him cool water to drink.
text.p06: Willo gave her shade on hot days, and his birds sang her to sleep at night.
text.p07: "Where does all my water go?" Nura asked one evening. "Down to everything," said Willo.
text.p08: Nura looked at the huge valley below. "If I run all the way down there, I'll spread out thin and disappear."
text.p09: Then one spring night, a storm came. Crash! Rumble! Rocks tumbled across Nura's little stream.
text.p10: Nura could have pushed her way through. But she thought, "Now I can keep all of me."
text.p11: Nura grew and grew into a big, round pond. She held the whole sky inside her.
text.p12: "Look how much I have!" she said proudly. "And all of it is mine."
text.p13: But day after day, Nura didn't move. She grew still… and quiet… and very, very heavy.
text.p14: Leaves sank. Her sparkle faded to a murky green. One by one, the frogs hopped away.
text.p15: Far below, the stream bed dried up. The meadow turned crunchy and brown.
text.p16: The otters searched for a swimming hole. The bees buzzed from dry flower to dry flower.
text.p17: Just below the rocks, Willo began to droop. His leaves turned yellow and fell.
text.p18: His birds flew away to find water. "Willo?" whispered Nura. But he was too thirsty to answer.
text.p19: Nura had more water than ever before. So why did she feel so empty?
text.p20: She was full, but she was lonely. She was big, but she felt very small.
text.p21: That night, Grandmother Cloud drifted down and rested on the mountain beside her.
text.p22: "You were never only yours, little one. You were snow we gave the mountain. Gifts are meant to keep moving."
text.p23: Nura took a deep breath. She gathered all her water… and spilled over the wall! Whoosh!
text.p24: Down she tumbled, sparkling in the sun again. Willo drank and drank, and his leaves lifted up.
text.p25: Splash! The otter kits leaped in. The bees sipped. The meadow turned green again.
text.p26: Flowers opened. The field mice filled their buckets for their gardens. The whole valley came alive.
text.p27: Nura flowed on, past the mill and through the orchard. Other little streams joined her along the way.
text.p28: She wasn't getting smaller. She was becoming a river, and a part of everything she touched.
text.p29: At last she reached the sea. The warm sun lifted her up, up, up into the sky.
text.p30: Now she was a little cloud beside Grandmother Cloud, looking down at the green valley she had helped.
text.p31: One quiet winter night, she fell as soft snow on her very own mountain.
text.p32: In spring, she bubbled up fresh and new, beside a blossoming Willo. Water that is held grows still. Water that is shared stays alive. The End
text.cover: The Spring That Wanted to Stay. A Story About Generosity and the Gifts We Pass On
